fatal_errors: The proposed 5 at.% Al addition does not reconstruct the target intervention of 4.2 at.% Cr in as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The assumed single-phase FCC starting material conflicts with the target single-phase BCC HfMoTaTiZr alloy.
The hypothesized coherent precipitates are unsupported and omit the target reticulated multicomponent Laves phase.
No prior-study evidence or citations support the claimed 20% high-temperature improvement.
The experiment does not test preservation of room-temperature performance and does not establish a processing-matched baseline.

The falsification thresholds are inconsistent with the stated hypothesis: a claim of 20% improvement and less than 2% density increase is not falsified until improvement falls below 10% or density rises above 3%.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad turbine-alloy goals of high-temperature capability, density control, and room-temperature retention, but it has essentially no reconstruction agreement with the hidden target. The target concerns Cr-modified BCC HfMoTaTiZr tested in room-temperature compression, where about 3.8–4 vol.% of a reticulated Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves phase and Cr-induced lattice contraction jointly increase yield strength and fracture strain. The generated proposal instead assumes an unspecified FCC refractory alloy, Al addition, coherent precipitation, and 1000°C tensile loading. Its mechanism is generic, its baseline is not compositionally or processing-defined, and no evidence supports coherent precipitate formation or the numerical performance claim. The proposed experiment is only weakly discriminating because loading at a nominal 100 MPa does not by itself determine yield strength, room-temperature strength or ductility is not measured, and the falsification rule tolerates outcomes that already violate the hypothesis.
